finding.evidence: On new chat.create, only `existing.abort()` is called. Unlike chat.abort (message-router.ts:728-745) there is no `rejectPendingForThread`, `securityConfirmations.rejectForWorker`, or computer-task flip. Extension dispatch Promise in server.ts:2196-2314 never observes AbortSignal — only pending map rejection ends it. Mid-CDP tools run until 15s timeout; L2 dialogs can sit until confirmation timeout; concurrent new chat can race in-flight tools.
finding.fix_hint: On supersede (and any abortThreadChat caller), also call rejectPendingForThread(threadId), securityConfirmations.rejectForWorker(threadId), flipAllComputerTaskAborts, and wire signal.abort into extension pending resolvers.
finding.impact: Stop-by-resend leaves browser CDP and confirmation UI live; user believes prior run stopped while tools continue executing on real tabs.
finding.title: chat.create supersede aborts LLM only — does not drain extension tools or L2

verdict.evidence: message-router.ts chat.create:433-438 only existing.abort(); chat.abort:728-754 does rejectForWorker + rejectPendingForThread + lease release; server.ts:5466-5473 flipAllComputerTaskAborts only on chat.abort; server.ts createToolExecutor extension Promise ~2196-2314 no AbortSignal listener (pendingToolCalls + timeout only); TOOL_EXECUTION_TIMEOUT_MS=15000; adapter passes signal to executeTool but extension path ignores it; App.tsx handleSend→chat.send→chat.create, handleStop→chat.abort.
verdict.reason: Confirmed asymmetry: chat.create supersede only calls existing.abort() on the thread AbortController; unlike chat.abort it never rejectPendingForThread, rejectForWorker, releaseLeases, or flipAllComputerTaskAborts. Extension tool.execute Promise does not observe AbortSignal (only pending map rejection/timeout ends it); MCP alone honors signal. UI resend uses chat.create without prior chat.abort, so mid-CDP tools, L2 dialogs (45s), and host_computer can continue while a new run starts. Explicit Stop (chat.abort) does full drain—so impact is supersede/resend residual, not broken Stop—hence medium not high.

finding.evidence: createToolResultMessage stores `content: JSON.stringify(result)` and `tool_calls: [{ params, result }]` with no redaction. adapter.ts:807 `threadManager.addMessage(...)` writes that to ~/.cmspark-agent/threads. history/store.ts:83-126 redacts cookies/evaluate/MCP/shell for history.db only — threads are the durable conversation used by rebuildMessagesFromHistory.
finding.fix_hint: Apply the same redactForStorage policy (or stronger) before addMessage for tool rows; keep full results only ephemerally for the current LLM round if needed.
finding.impact: Cookie values, evaluate outputs, shell stdout, MCP file reads, and secrets remain on disk in thread JSON; export/backup/filesystem access can exfiltrate session material that history.db intentionally strips.
finding.title: Thread message store persists full unredacted tool params and results

verdict.evidence: adapter.ts:119-130 createToolResultMessage sets content: JSON.stringify(result) and tool_calls:[{params, result}] with no redaction; adapter.ts:807 threadManager.addMessage(threadId, createToolResultMessage(...)); adapter.ts:203-211 rebuildMessagesFromHistory uses JSON.stringify(tc.result). history/store.ts:22-35 SENSITIVE_COOKIE_TOOLS/SENSITIVE_CODE_TOOLS + shell_exec; store.ts:442-448 redactForStorage only on history.db record(). thread-manager.ts:503-530 addMessage pushes raw message then atomicWriteJSON (io.ts:16 default 0o600). markdown-export.ts renderToolEntry only length-bounds JSON (MAX_RESULT_JSON_LEN=2000), no secret redaction.
verdict.reason: Confirmed: createToolResultMessage + threadManager.addMessage persist full unredacted tool params/results to ~/.cmspark-agent/threads/*.json; rebuildMessagesFromHistory consumes tc.result from that store. history/store.ts redactForStorage redacts cookies/code/MCP/shell for history.db only — intentional asymmetry. Mitigations (0o600 atomicWriteJSON, functional need for multi-turn LLM) reduce multi-user exposure but do not remove durable cookie/session and secret material from thread JSON or length-bounded exports. Impact for get_cookies and sensitive MCP reads matches the session-hijack threat history.db was fixed for.

finding.evidence: adapter: `if (mcpSelectionMode === "manual") { mcpTools = mcpManager.getAggregatedToolsForServers(activeServerIds) }` — visibility only. executeMcpTool: `const route = manager.resolveToolName(toolName)` uses full `aggregated.aliases` with no thread/active_mcp_server_ids check. Manager comment admits aliases exist so router can dispatch; selection never re-checked at call time.
finding.fix_hint: In executeMcpTool (and executeMcpMetaTool), load acting thread mcp_selection_mode/active_mcp_server_ids; if manual, reject when route.serverName not in active set. Mirror isToolAllowed hard-gate style.
finding.impact: Thread marked manual with a subset of servers can still execute tools on any connected server if the model invents/recalls a namespaced name (or pack/tool_whitelist does not list exact mcp__ names). Undermines intended isolation between MCP servers.
finding.title: Per-thread mcp_selection_mode=manual only filters LLM tool list, not execute path

verdict.evidence: adapter.ts:432-436: if (mcpSelectionMode === "manual") { mcpTools = mcpManager.getAggregatedToolsForServers(activeServerIds) } else { mcpTools = mcpManager.getAggregatedTools() }. manager.ts:297-312: getAggregatedToolsForServers only returns filtered definitions; resolveToolName uses this.aggregated.aliases.get(namespacedName) with no server allow-list. manager.ts:291-293 falsely claims dropped aliases mean "the router can't dispatch". server.ts:2182-2184: isMcpNamespaced → executeMcpTool with no thread selection gate. server.ts:4033-4037: route = manager.resolveToolName(toolName); only fails if not found. thread-manager.ts:554-558: isToolAllowed returns true when tool_whitelist is null (default).
verdict.reason: Confirmed: mcp_selection_mode=manual only filters LLM tool definitions in adapter.ts; executeMcpTool resolves via full aggregated.aliases with no thread/active_mcp_server_ids check. Manager comment claiming aliases are dropped so the router cannot dispatch is false. Impact is real for default threads (tool_whitelist=null) if the model invents/recalls mcp__ names, but lower than claimed high: pack allowlists hard-block unlisted names via isToolAllowed, and trust/capability confirms still gate many calls. Original audit item 7 was visibility-only by design.

finding.evidence: McpServerMeta.config documents: "Sensitive values (env, headers) included". mcp.list returns `getMcpManager().listServers()` with full config. servers_updated broadcasts metas/listServers() unredacted. By contrast redactConfigForBroadcast masks mcp.servers env/headers values to "***" for config.updated.
finding.fix_hint: Reuse redactConfigForBroadcast-style masking when serializing McpServerMeta for WS; keep plaintext only for local disk/edit apply path, not outbound list/status events.
finding.impact: Any authenticated WS peer (multi-panel / multi-peer) receives API keys and Authorization headers configured for MCP HTTP/stdio servers, defeating the redaction applied on config.updated.
finding.title: mcp.list / mcp.servers.updated broadcast unredacted env and headers

verdict.evidence: types.ts:109-112 documents "Sensitive values (env, headers) included"; client.ts:81 config: { ...this._config }; message-router.ts:1074-1076 mcp.list → listServers(); server.ts:5209-5216 broadcastToClients({ type: "mcp.servers.updated", servers: metas|listServers() }) with no redact; server.ts:4568-4615 + 5292-5294 redactConfigForBroadcast masks env/headers only on config.updated. No mcp.list/servers_updated redaction tests; config-broadcast-redact.test.ts covers only config.updated path.
verdict.reason: Confirmed by reading current code: McpServerMeta intentionally embeds full McpServerConfig; client.getMeta() shallow-copies _config (env/headers); mcp.list and mcp.add/update/delete/toggle responses return getMcpManager().listServers() unredacted; servers_updated/tools_changed broadcast metas/listServers() via broadcastToClients with no redaction. By contrast config.updated uses redactConfigForBroadcast which masks mcp.servers env/headers values to "***". Mitigations: only authenticated peers receive broadcasts, WS is loopback, and UI edit form depends on plaintext—so not unauthenticated RCE-class exposure, but multi-peer still receives secrets and that defeats SRV-1-style redaction. Severity lowered from high to medium for auth+loopback boundary.

Adapter still passes "--check-occlusion". postEventDual clears process pin and event.post(.cghidEventTap) so HID delivers to frontmost window under cursor after activate.

Prefer SkyLight-only when trusted, or require FG raise success before HID. Add unit/integration tests that assert flag rejects covered coordinates.
finding.impact: TS layer believes click occlusion is enforced; when Chrome/side panel or another window covers the target, inject can still report ok while the physical click lands on a non-whitelisted UI (documented b0faek/psl8ci class). Trust-root for "I only authorized WeChat" is weakened.
finding.title: macOS --check-occlusion / --check-onscreen are dead flags; HID dual-post can misroute clicks

verdict.evidence: host.swift:1689-1691 cuInject only uses checkSecureInput + estopFlag; checkOcclusion/checkOnscreen never read in body (grep: only signature+argv at :687). host.swift:1675-1686 postEventDual sets eventTargetUnixProcessID=0 then event.post(.cghidEventTap); success = skyOk || useHid. darwin-adapters.ts:715-718 click always passes --check-occlusion; :743-746 type passes --check-onscreen; :702-708 preferForeground swallows non-probe raise failures. host.swift:1040 comment claims '--check-occlusion on inject' handles occlusion; :1706 host still _ = cuActivatePid(pid). Contrast Windows computer-input.ps1:321-331 Assert-Landing WindowFromPoint OCCLUDED fail-closed. host-skylight.swift:1104-1106 same dead params.
verdict.reason: Independently confirmed: cuInject accepts checkOcclusion/checkOnscreen but only gates on checkSecureInput and estopFlag; darwin-adapters still pass --check-occlusion/--check-onscreen; comments falsely claim occlusion defense-in-depth. postEventDual clears PID pin and HID-posts, so residual overlay/FG-race misroute is real—especially with preferForeground swallowing FOREGROUND_RAISE_FAILED and host ignoring cuActivatePid result. Not high: SkyLight remains PID-pinned, host activates before inject by default, and computer-use L2/whitelist still gate tool invocation; Windows has real WindowFromPoint OCCLUDED, Darwin does not. Impact is false safety contract + residual misroute, not unconstrained off-whitelist inject.

finding.evidence: func cuPidForWindow: CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo([.optionAll], windowId) then windows.first for PID. Sibling cuWindowInfoDict correctly searches by kCGWindowNumber; inject/activate paths call cuPidForWindow instead.
finding.fix_hint: Resolve PID via cuWindowInfoDict(windowId:)[kCGWindowOwnerPID]; fail closed if missing. Share one resolver with screenshot/AX paths.
finding.impact: SkyLight pin and cuActivatePid may target the wrong process (often frontmost/z-order head). Compounds COMP-1 HID misroute and FOREGROUND races after side-panel Allow.
finding.title: cuPidForWindow ignores windowId — uses first CGWindowList entry under optionAll

verdict.reason: cuPidForWindow calls CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo([.optionAll], windowId) and returns windows.first's kCGWindowOwnerPID without matching kCGWindowNumber. With optionAll, relativeToWindow does not filter; first entry is front-to-back head (usually frontmost). Sibling cuWindowInfoDict correctly filters by id and comments ban unfiltered optionAll. inject/activate/AX/screenshot paths all use the broken helper (duplicated in host-skylight.swift). After Side Panel Allow, frontmost is often Chrome, so SkyLight pin and cuActivatePid can target the wrong process. No tests or flags mitigate this.

finding.evidence: ensureForeground throws FOREGROUND_RAISE_FAILED when raise fails; preferForeground only rethrows ForegroundProbeBrokenError and swallows raise failure. click/type/key call preferForeground then inject. Comments admit type/key lack occlusion guard.
finding.fix_hint: Fail closed on FOREGROUND_RAISE_FAILED for injective actions, or re-L2; only soft-skip when SkyLight-only delivery is verified and occlusion check passes.
finding.impact: Product tradeoff for WeChat key-window reliability becomes fail-open: inject proceeds without confirmed frontmost target, amplifying mis-click/type under Chrome contention.
finding.title: preferForeground soft-fails FOREGROUND_RAISE_FAILED then still injects

verdict.evidence: darwin-adapters.ts preferForeground: try { await this.ensureForeground(hwnd) } catch (err) { if (err instanceof ForegroundProbeBrokenError) throw err } — FOREGROUND_RAISE_FAILED not rethrown. ensureForeground on !raised: throw new ComputerError("FOREGROUND_RAISE_FAILED", ...). click/typeText/keyChord: await this.preferForeground(hwnd) then inject. preferForeground comment: "Soft-best-effort: raise failure does not block inject except hard probe-broken." types.ts FOREGROUND_RAISE_FAILED: "Precondition guard failed → inject must NOT proceed." host.swift cuInject: _ = cuActivatePid(pid) then postEventDual (SkyLight+HID); checkOcclusion parameter never read.
verdict.reason: Confirmed: preferForeground catches ensureForeground errors and rethrows only ForegroundProbeBrokenError, so ComputerError(FOREGROUND_RAISE_FAILED) is swallowed and click/typeText/keyChord still inject. That contradicts types.ts ('inject must NOT proceed') and the product brief (surface FOREGROUND_RAISE_FAILED). Impact is real under Chrome contention because host inject dual-posts HID to frontmost-under-cursor after a weak cuActivatePid, while companion osascript raise is the stronger path already failed. Not full high/refuted: soft-best-effort is an explicit product comment, probe-broken still fail-closed, and host always attempts activate. Darwin --check-occlusion is a dead flag (unused in host.swift/host-skylight.swift), so click is not better-guarded than type/key.

finding.evidence: private threadFilePath(threadId: string): string { return path.join(getConfigDir(), "threads", `${threadId}.json`) } — only create() calls sanitizeId (alphanumeric/hyphen/underscore). getMessages/addMessage/updateMessage/deleteMessagesFrom/delete use raw threadId. path.join normalizes '..', so thread_id '../config' resolves to ~/.cmspark-agent/config.json; addMessage atomicWriteJSON would overwrite it with {messages:[...]}; delete would unlinkSync it. message-router passes rest.thread_id through without sanitization.
finding.fix_hint: Resolve path and require realpath containment under threads/; or apply sanitizeId (reject '..' / path seps) in threadFilePath for ALL readers/writers, not only create().
finding.impact: Authenticated peer (or compromised extension holding ws_secret) can corrupt or delete config.json / other DATA_DIR JSON via crafted thread_id on message or delete APIs — silent data loss of API keys, domains, MCP/apps config.
finding.title: threadFilePath does not sanitize thread_id — path escape under DATA_DIR

verdict.evidence: companion/src/threads/thread-manager.ts:242-244 threadFilePath = path.join(getConfigDir(),'threads',`${threadId}.json`) with no sanitize; 265-269 sanitizeId only used at create() line 275; delete() 312-315 filter+saveIndex then unlinkSync(threadFilePath(threadId)) even if id absent; addMessage 510-530 read-or-empty then atomicWriteJSON(filePath). message-router.ts thread.delete: threadManager.delete(rest.thread_id) no check. server.ts thread.delete validator: only typeof string. adapter chatCreate line 292 addMessage(threadId) without existence gate.
verdict.reason: Confirmed: threadFilePath joins unsanitized threadId; sanitizeId only in create(). delete() always unlinkSync(threadFilePath) with no index membership check; message-router thread.delete and server schema pass any non-empty string. path.join normalizes '..' so thread_id '../config' → DATA_DIR/config.json (delete or addMessage overwrite with {messages}); 'index' hits threads/index.json. Auth required (ws_secret) and config.set already exists, but this bypasses config validation and enables silent delete/corrupt of arbitrary reachable *.json — still high integrity impact.

finding.title: No Developer ID / notarization / Authenticode on ship artifacts

verdict.evidence: scripts/create-dmg.sh:104-106: `codesign --force --deep --sign - --options runtime` (ad-hoc). .github/workflows/release.yml:163-167: binaries are **not** Developer ID–codesigned / notarized / Authenticode-signed (pending certificates). scripts/build-windows-exe.ps1:156-165: `signtool remove /s` only when present; never `signtool sign`. No notarytool/Developer ID Application/`signtool sign` in ship pipeline.
verdict.reason: Confirmed: create-dmg.sh uses ad-hoc codesign only (`--sign -`); release.yml explicitly states no Developer ID/notarization/Authenticode; build-windows-exe.ps1 only removes signatures via signtool and never signs. No notarytool/signtool-sign/Developer ID path exists in CI. Impact is real (Gatekeeper/SmartScreen friction; ad-hoc reinstall can churn TCC CDHash) but is known, disclosed, partially mitigated by ad-hoc deep-sign for local TCC, and intentionally deferred (D9/P1 cert procurement)—not a runtime exploit path. Severity lowered from high to medium.

finding.evidence: Test comment: "The production gate lives inside startServer()'s connection handler, which NO test calls directly". startAuthedServer() reimplements challenge/handshake/terminate. Production: "Keep in sync with ... ws-auth-handshake.test.ts (which replicates this exact gate, since no test calls startServer())".
finding.fix_hint: Add one ephemeral-port integration that boots real startServer (or extract connection handler and unit/integration test the production function once), then delete the replica over time.
finding.impact: A drift in startServer wiring (message order, markPaired, computer.state push, ping keepalive, pre-auth harvest) can ship while replica tests stay green — highest remaining trust-root coverage hole.
finding.title: startServer() never called; WS auth gate is a test-side replica

verdict.evidence: Test header (ws-auth-handshake.test.ts:7-12): "production gate lives inside startServer()'s connection handler, which NO test calls directly" / "we replicate the auth gate here". Replica startAuthedServer (L178-231) only does issueChallenge→verifyProof→auth.ok+connected; no markPaired/computer.state/size/validateWsMessage/idempotent handshake/ping. Production (server.ts:5306-5435) has full gate including markPaired() + computer.state push; comment L5391-5392 admits replica. Grep of companion/tests: zero startServer() call sites; only extracted helpers imported from server.ts. Crypto unit-tested via production imports (L28-53, L128-166); markPaired covered in ws-auth-paired-marker.test.ts.
verdict.reason: Confirmed: no test calls startServer(); ws-auth-handshake uses a bare-wss replica explicitly documented as out of sync risk with production connection-handler wiring (markPaired, computer.state, validateWsMessage order, ping, idempotent handshake). Not a production vulnerability: crypto and proof verify run against real ws-auth modules; pre-auth reject/wrong-proof/happy-path are covered by the replica; markPaired has separate unit tests. High is inflated for known intentional dual-maintenance coverage debt.

finding.evidence: Static import createToolExecutor from server with no _*-setup; mockWs() only {readyState:1, send:noop}. Comment admits confirmation "times out at the 45s confirmation gate"; only assert success===false. DEFAULT_SECURITY_CONFIRMATION_TIMEOUT_MS = 45000.
finding.fix_hint: Reuse security-gates harness (real WS + CMSPARK_DATA_DIR setup); assert confirmation.request emitted and deny/timeout with short timeoutMs injection; never rely on 45s default.
finding.impact: On default config CI pays ~45s hang; on a developer machine whose real DATA_DIR has auto_approve_dangerous, behavior diverges. Weak assertion cannot pin strip-vs-invalid-token contract beyond "didn't succeed".
finding.title: evaluate-token integration uses mock WS, no DATA_DIR isolation, can block 45s

verdict.evidence: evaluate-token.test.ts: import createToolExecutor with no _*-setup; mockWs={readyState:1,send:noop}; only assert.equal(result.success,false); comments admit 45s confirm hang. server.ts: strip LLM security_token then L2 if !security_token; readyState!==OPEN → unavailable (dead for this mock); else securityConfirmations.request. security-confirmation.ts: DEFAULT_SECURITY_CONFIRMATION_TIMEOUT_MS=45000 used by manager constructor + setTimeout. This machine ~/.cmspark-agent/config.json has auto_approve_dangerous:true and allow_all_schemes:true (path divergence). Mitigations: tests/integration/_security-gates-setup.ts + security-gates.test.ts W8 cases (host_read + evaluate replay) assert confirmation.request after strip with isolated DATA_DIR.
verdict.reason: The first evaluate-token integration case is genuinely weak and slow: mockWs sets readyState=1 so L2 confirmation runs and defaults to DEFAULT_SECURITY_CONFIRMATION_TIMEOUT_MS (45s); there is no CMSPARK_DATA_DIR setup (unlike security-gates), so real auto_approve_dangerous/allow_all_schemes can divert the path (e.g. 15s tool dispatch timeout) while still asserting only success===false. That assert cannot distinguish W8 strip→gate from the pre-strip Invalid-token reject for a bogus token. Severity is not high: this is test hygiene/CI tax, not a product bug, and security-gates already pins evaluate strip with isolated DATA_DIR, real WS, and confirmation.request observation. The H2 issueToken/validateToken unit case in the same file is fine.

Cross-cutting regressions (originWs inconsistency SEC-1, abort incompleteness) cluster here because there is no session/tool-admission kernel with clear module boundaries.
finding.title: server.ts owns auth, every L2 gate, companion tools, MCP, CU, and lifecycle (~5782 LOC)

verdict.evidence: companion/src/server.ts L5781 setupGracefulShutdown; L494 export function createToolExecutor; L579-605 isToolAllowed/pack gate; L629-652 tab lease HARD; L687-721 COOKIE_TOOLS; L790-818 L2_GATE_TOOLS + forceConfirm path; L2105-2123 executeCompanionTool + originWs-bound securityConfirmations.request; L2705-4015 executeCompanionTool switch (spawn_worker…host_computer); L4025 executeMcpTool; L4654 validateWsMessage; L5092 startServer; L193/299 pendingToolCalls + securityConfirmations. docs/architecture.md L157-160: 'Tool Executor (companion/src/server.ts)'. Mitigations: imports from ./ws-auth, ./security-confirmation, ./security-policy, ./mcp, dynamic import ./orchestrator, ./board, ./packs; createToolExecutor exported and unit-tested without full startServer. message-router.ts: handleMessage ends ~L2342 with ~96 case arms (separate file, not all in server.ts).
verdict.reason: Confirmed: server.ts is a ~5782-LOC composition root; createToolExecutor mixes pack whitelist, tab leases, L2_GATE_TOOLS, confirmation, MCP/extension dispatch; executeCompanionTool is a large switch; architecture.md documents Tool Executor here; message-router is a second large case-switch. Severity is not high: domain logic is largely extracted (ws-auth, security-confirmation/policy, mcp/, orchestrator/, board/, host-use/, computer/, capability/), createToolExecutor is intentionally the single admission SoT (not 'no kernel'), and many tests exercise createToolExecutor without startServer. This is maintainability/blast-radius debt, not an unmitigated high-severity defect.

finding.evidence: Supersede only aborts controller then starts a new chatCreate on the same thread without awaiting the old run: `existing.abort(); abortControllers.delete(...);` then later `await chatCreate(...)`. Old run finally always does `abortControllers.delete(rest.thread_id); releaseMultiAgentLlmLoop(rest.thread_id)` — not generation-guarded, so it deletes the *new* controller and releases a multi-agent slot still held by the successor. On AbortError, adapter `deleteMessagesFrom(threadId, savedAssistantId)` slices from the old assistant inclusive, which also drops any user/tool messages the successor already appended after that id. Catch also sends `chat.aborted` for the thread while the new stream may still be live; extension applies SET_PROCESSING false + "⏹ 已停止生成" with only thread_id gate (no run id).
finding.fix_hint: Per-thread generation token (or AbortController identity): finally only deletes/releases if map entry === this run’s controller. Join supersede: await prior chatCreate settle (or rejectPendingForThread + wait tools) before new user message. Scope deleteMessagesFrom to messages owned by the aborted run (ids recorded this generation), not “everything after old assistant”. Stamp chat.aborted/done/error with run_id and ignore stale events in the extension.
finding.impact: Resend/stop-by-resend during in-flight tools can: make the new turn un-abortable; free multi-agent LLM cap early (over-admit workers); delete the new user message and partial tape from disk; flash false stop UI while generation continues. Data loss + control-plane desync under normal multi-turn use.
finding.title: chat.create supersede: predecessor finally clobbers successor abort, multi-agent gate, and can wipe new messages

verdict.evidence: message-router.ts chat.create: existing.abort(); abortControllers.delete; set new controller; finally { abortControllers.delete(rest.thread_id); releaseMultiAgentLlmLoop(rest.thread_id) } and catch sends chat.aborted for thread_id only. llm-loop-gate: re-entrant tryAcquire if holders.has(threadId); release deletes holder without generation. adapter AbortError path: threadManager.deleteMessagesFrom(threadId, savedAssistantId). thread-manager deleteMessagesFrom: data.messages = messages.slice(0, idx). useWebSocket chat.aborted: SET_PROCESSING false + ⏹ 已停止生成 with shouldApplyStreamEvent(thread_id) only. server.ts browser tool Promise path does not wire signal abort. App canSend = !isStreaming && ... (not !isProcessing).
verdict.reason: Independently confirmed: chat.create supersede aborts the prior run then installs a new AbortController/gate slot with no generation ownership. Predecessor finally always abortControllers.delete(thread_id) and releaseMultiAgentLlmLoop(thread_id), clobbering the successor controller and freeing the multi-agent LLM cap while the new loop still runs. On AbortError, adapter deleteMessagesFrom(savedAssistantId) slices the tape from the old assistant inclusive with no run guard, so a successor user/tool messages appended after that id can be wiped—especially while in-flight CDP tools ignore signal and delay unwind. Catch also emits chat.aborted gated only by thread_id; extension clears isProcessing and injects ⏹ 已停止生成 while the successor stream may still be live. Concurrent WS handleMessage is unserialized; UI canSend does not block isProcessing, so resend during tools is a normal path. No generation-id/CAS mitigations found.

finding.evidence: pendingToolCalls entries store resolve/timer/thread_id/tabId but not owning WebSocket. On every `ws.on("close")`: `applyConnectionCloseGracePeriod()` iterates **all** pending ids, clears their timers, and after WS_DISCONNECT_GRACE_MS=5000 resolves `{ success: false, error: "WebSocket disconnected" }`. Contrast `securityConfirmations.rejectAll("disconnect", ws)` which scopes by originWs. Default tool timeout is 15s; browser_download dispatch timeout can be up to ~125s — far above the 5s grace. Tray Origin `cmspark-tray://local` is an always-on second peer.
finding.fix_hint: Stamp each pendingToolCall with `originWs` (the socket tool.execute was sent on). On close, only grace-kill entries for that ws. Optionally push tool.cancel to that peer only. Keep global grace only for process shutdown.
finding.impact: Tray or secondary panel disconnect/reconnect while extension tools run falsely fails navigate/evaluate/download mid-flight; long downloads especially. Can strand agent loops with fake WS errors despite extension still connected.
finding.title: applyConnectionCloseGracePeriod is global — any peer disconnect kills all pending tools

verdict.evidence: companion/src/server.ts pendingToolCalls Map fields are only resolve/reject/timer/thread_id/tabId/tool_name (lines 193-201) — no ws. Registration at 2283-2290 omits owner socket though tool.execute is unicast to a specific ws. applyConnectionCloseGracePeriod (2657-2668) iterates all pendingToolCalls, clearTimeout, setTimeout 5000ms → resolve WebSocket disconnected. ws.on('close') (5670-5680): clients.delete(ws); applyConnectionCloseGracePeriod(); securityConfirmations.rejectAll('disconnect', ws) — tools unscoped, confirmations scoped. resolveToolDispatchTimeoutMs: default 15000, browser_download up to BROWSER_DOWNLOAD_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS+5000 (102-112). isAllowedWsOrigin accepts cmspark-tray://local (138). security-confirmation.ts rejectAll documents multi-client fix C-SRV-1 (505-533).
verdict.reason: Confirmed by reading current server.ts: pendingToolCalls stores no owner WebSocket; every ws.on('close') unconditionally calls applyConnectionCloseGracePeriod() which clears/replaces timers for ALL pending ids and after WS_DISCONNECT_GRACE_MS=5000 resolves {success:false, error:'WebSocket disconnected'}. securityConfirmations.rejectAll('disconnect', ws) is correctly origin-scoped (C-SRV-1); tools are not. Tray origin cmspark-tray://local is a designed second peer with reconnect/heartbeat closes. Default tool timeout 15s and browser_download up to ~125s far exceed the global 5s grace, so a non-executor peer disconnect can fail in-flight extension tools while the extension socket is still open. No clients.size===0 gate, no feature flag, no fix in tests (they only assert global grace behavior).

finding.evidence: mcp.add: `replaceMcpServers(newServers)` with only validateMcpServerConfig (command string + trust_level). configEvents → `await mcpManager.applyConfig(updatedConfig.mcp)`. createTransport stdio: `new StdioClientTransport({ command: config.command, args, env, cwd })` — no securityConfirmations.request. Contrast shell_exec which requires module + security_token L2.
finding.fix_hint: Require L2 (or security arm phrase) for mcp.add/update when transport=stdio or when command/args/cwd/env change; optionally allowlist command basenames; never auto-enable mcp.enabled on first add without confirm.
finding.impact: Any authenticated WS peer (compromised extension, stolen pairing secret, second panel) can register `command: "/bin/bash"` (or any binary) and get companion to spawn it as the user, without enterprise shell module, forceConfirm, or arm phrase — local RCE as companion uid.
finding.title: mcp.add stdio spawns arbitrary local command without L2 (bypasses shell enterprise gate)

verdict.evidence: message-router.ts mcp.add: validateMcpServerConfig then replaceMcpServers; auto setMcpEnabled(true) when wasEmpty. validateMcpServerConfig stdio: only requires typeof command==='string' (no allowlist). server.ts configEvents: await mcpManager.applyConfig(updatedConfig.mcp). manager applyConfig: if (cfg.enabled) this.startClient(...). transport.ts: new StdioClientTransport({ command: config.command, args, env, cwd }). Contrast shell_exec: requireModule('shell') + security_token L2 (server.ts ~3160-3165; capability/shell.ts requireModule). apps/guards.ts LOLBIN_BASENAMES documents add-time silent RCE as #1 threat — no analog on MCP path. ws-auth requires handshake for mcp.add but treats post-auth mcp.add as allowed control plane.
verdict.reason: Independently confirmed: authenticated WS mcp.add only runs validateMcpServerConfig (command string + trust_level shape), then replaceMcpServers → CONFIG_CHANGE_EVENT → mcpManager.applyConfig → startClient → createTransport StdioClientTransport({command}) with no securityConfirmations.request, no shell requireModule, no L2 security_token, and no apps-style LOLBIN denylist. First-server auto setMcpEnabled(true) makes spawn even more likely. Auth/pairing blocks unauthenticated peers but does not restore the shell enterprise/L2 gates shell_exec requires; same class of add-time arbitrary spawn that apps.guards explicitly hard-denies. Not critical because loopback+pairing is required.

executive_summary: CMspark 0.3.0 re-audit (2026-07-25) after computer-use v1.3 + security P0 batches. Prior 2026-07-09 score 4.4/C with 4 Criticals is FIXED_VERIFY: WS HMAC+Origin (C1), history.db flush (C2), CI hard-gates without || true (C3), prod npm audit (C4). Adversarial pass: 0 surviving Criticals. Overall 5.8/C+ (+1.4). Residual 10 confirmed High: (1) threadFilePath path escape can delete/overwrite config under DATA_DIR; (2) mcp.add stdio spawns arbitrary local command without L2/shell module; (3) threads/*.json store unredacted tool params/results (cookies/shell/MCP/evaluate) bypassing history.db redaction; (4) chat.create supersede predecessor finally clobbers successor AbortController/multi-agent gate and can wipe new messages; (5) applyConnectionCloseGracePeriod is global—any peer disconnect kills all pending tools; (6) macOS cuPidForWindow ignores windowId (first CGWindowList entry); (7) HUD spike uses privileged respond() when CMSPARK_HUD_SPIKE=1; (8) no tool.cancel / analyze_image pending lacks thread_id so Stop cannot fully halt CDP/vision; (9) tray autostart launchd args diverge from install-daemon.sh and may never start companion; (10) MCP list unredacted env/headers + stdio children inherit full process.env/user-env. Product is no longer trust-root-broken, but not public-release-safe until P0 batches land.
